basic_information.name: smolagents
basic_information.creator: Hugging Face — led by Aymeric Roucher (Project Lead on Agents), with Albert Villanova del Moral, Thomas Wolf (co-founder & CSO), Leandro von Werra, and Erik Kaunismäki
basic_information.release_date: December 31, 2024 (initial public release; repository created December 5, 2024). Successor to transformers.agents.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: code_first | single_agent | multi_agent — smolagents is built around the code-first paradigm: CodeAgent writes its actions as Python code (function calls, loops, conditionals) rather than JSON tool-call specifications. This yields ~30% fewer steps and LLM calls on complex benchmarks. Also supports ToolCallingAgent for standard JSON/text-based tool calling. Multi-agent orchestration via ManagedAgent wrapper enables hierarchical manager/worker patterns. Core logic fits in ~1,000 lines of code with minimal abstractions.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Model-agnostic. Supports any LLM via multiple integration paths: (1) Hugging Face Hub models via InferenceClientModel with Inference Providers (Hugging Face, Together, Replicate, etc.), (2) OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100+ providers via LiteLLMModel integration, (3) Local models via TransformersModel (Hugging Face Transformers) or Ollama. Each agent can use a different model. Default model is available through Hugging Face Inference API.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Highly flexible tool-agnostic approach. Tools can come from: (1) Custom Python functions decorated with @tool or classes inheriting from Tool, (2) Any MCP server via ToolCollection.from_mcp() — supports latest MCP specs including outputSchema for structured returns, (3) LangChain tools via Tool.from_langchain(), (4) Hugging Face Hub Gradio Spaces via Tool.from_space() — thousands of existing Spaces become instant agent tools, (5) Built-in tools like DuckDuckGoSearchTool, VisitWebpageTool, etc. Tools can be shared/loaded to/from the Hub.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) — agents alternate between reasoning traces (thoughts) and actions in an interleaved multi-step loop. CodeAgent generates Python code as actions; the framework executes it and returns observations. The _run method manages periodic planning updates based on agent progress. Plans and facts are formatted and added to memory. Supports dynamic re-planning through step callbacks. Also supports plan customization with human-in-the-loop intervention via PlanningStep callbacks.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Yes — hierarchical multi-agent via ManagedAgent wrapper. A manager agent coordinates managed agents, each with their own tools and memory. Manager calls managed agents by generating Python code that invokes the agent method. Benefits: (1) Specialized tool sets per agent reduce tool selection errors, (2) Separate memories prevent context pollution (e.g., web search content stays out of code agent memory), (3) Modular design where instead of 1 agent with 10 tools, you have a manager + workers with 5 tools each. Supports nesting: managed agents can themselves have managed agents.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation) — agents maintain in-memory logs of each step via AgentMemory class. Each step produces memory entries including actions taken, observations received, errors encountered, and plans. Memory includes system_prompt, TaskStep, ActionStep (with step_number, observations, errors, observations_images), and PlanningStep. No built-in episodic, semantic, or procedural memory — the framework favors simplicity over built-in persistence.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: The agent converts its full memory into LLM-compatible format on each step, including all past actions, observations, errors, and plans. Over time this results in growing context size. Step callbacks can be used to prune memory (e.g., removing old screenshots from web browser agents to save tokens). A feature request for memory/history consolidation exists (GitHub Issue #901) but is not yet implemented. Developers can manually manage memory via agent.memory.steps access.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: in_memory — no built-in persistence across sessions. Memory exists only during an agent run. However, developers can serialize and transfer memory between agents (agent.memory.steps can be assigned from a previous agent's memory). Step-by-step execution mode allows manual memory manipulation between steps. External persistence can be implemented via step callbacks writing to databases or file systems.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Minimalist by design. Context is the full conversation history (system prompt + all steps). The framework provides hooks (step_callbacks, final_answer_callbacks) for developers to implement custom context engineering — e.g., pruning old observations, summarizing steps, or removing images. The replay() method allows inspecting past runs. Memory can be dynamically modified via callbacks that access the agent object. The philosophy is to keep the core simple and let developers customize context management for their specific use case.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Code-first agent execution: agents write Python code to invoke tools, enabling natural composability (function nesting, loops, conditionals) — ~30% more efficient than JSON tool calling. Two agent paradigms: CodeAgent (default, writes actions as Python code) and ToolCallingAgent (standard JSON/text-based tool calling). Multi-step reasoning via ReAct loop with configurable max_steps. Multi-agent orchestration via ManagedAgent hierarchies. Sandboxed code execution via Blaxel, E2B, Modal, Docker, or WebAssembly (Pyodide+Deno). Hub integration for sharing/loading tools and agents as Gradio Spaces. MCP server tool integration. LangChain tool compatibility. Step-by-step execution mode for granular control. Step callbacks and final answer callbacks for validation and human-in-the-loop. Plan customization with interactive human review. CLI tools (smolagent, webagent) for running agents without boilerplate. Vision web browser agent for multimodal web interaction. OpenTelemetry instrumentation for observability.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code, vision, video, audio inputs — multimodal via LLM capabilities. Vision web browser agent for screenshot-based web interaction. Image handling through observations_images in memory steps.
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop | fully_autonomous — configurable. Default: fully autonomous within max_steps limit. Human-in-the-loop via: (1) step_callbacks for pausing after plan creation (PlanningStep), (2) final_answer_callbacks for validating final answers before returning, (3) step-by-step execution mode for manual intervention between steps. No built-in approval workflow — developers implement oversight via callbacks.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Flexible and growing. Built-in tools: DuckDuckGoSearchTool, VisitWebpageTool, and others via smolagents[toolkit]. Any MCP server tools via ToolCollection.from_mcp(). LangChain tools via Tool.from_langchain(). Thousands of Hugging Face Hub Gradio Spaces usable as tools via Tool.from_space(). Custom tools via @tool decorator or Tool base class. Tools can be pushed to and loaded from the Hugging Face Hub. The smolagents organization on the Hub hosts community-shared tools.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Yes — first-class MCP support via ToolCollection.from_mcp(). Supports latest MCP specifications (2025-06-18+) including outputSchema for structured tool returns. Tools from any MCP server can be used by smolagents. Community examples and tutorials available for building MCP servers and clients with smolagents.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Community-supported — smolagents can be served with A2A protocol through the any-agent project. A community-built A2AMultiStepAgent wrapper inherits from smolagents.MultiStepAgent and delegates reasoning to remote A2A-compatible agents. Not a built-in first-party feature, but demonstrated interoperability with LangGraph agents via A2A. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: No explicit AGENTS.md support documented. smolagents uses its own system prompt and tool configuration approach. Agents are configured programmatically via Python code, not via project-level instruction files.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Strong interoperability. MCP support enables tool sharing with any MCP-compatible framework. LangChain tool compatibility via Tool.from_langchain(). A2A protocol support via community wrappers. Built on LiteLLM for universal LLM provider compatibility. Gradio Spaces integration connects to the broader Hugging Face ecosystem. Can consume tools from any framework that exposes MCP servers. OpenTelemetry support enables shared observability across frameworks.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: allow_list | sandbox — Multi-layered approach: (1) LocalPythonExecutor uses AST-based execution with explicit import authorization lists — imports are disallowed unless explicitly whitelisted, submodule access disabled by default, operation count capped to prevent infinite loops. (2) Remote sandboxing options: Blaxel (<25ms startup), E2B, Modal, Docker containers (with mem_limit, cpu_quota, pids_limit, no-new-privileges), or WebAssembly (Pyodide+Deno). (3) Docker setups can enforce minimal privileges (USER nobody, cap_drop ALL). The framework explicitly warns that no local sandbox is 100% secure — remote execution is recommended for high-security applications.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Via callbacks — step_callbacks can pause execution after plan creation for human review. final_answer_callbacks validate answers before returning. Step-by-step execution mode allows human intervention at every step. No built-in automatic escalation based on confidence thresholds — developers implement custom escalation logic via the callback system. Agents halt on max_steps limit if no final answer is reached.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Limited built-in support. final_answer_callbacks can implement custom validation checks on agent output. Structured output enforcement via code execution constrains agent actions to valid Python. Multi-agent review possible (one agent validates another's output). The code-first approach inherently reduces hallucination in tool usage because invalid code raises execution errors, providing immediate feedback. Error observations are fed back to the agent for self-correction. No built-in fact-checking or grounding mechanisms.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — via OpenTelemetry instrumentation. Every step is logged in AgentMemory with timing, observations, errors, and token usage. agent.replay() provides playback of past runs. Integration with Langfuse, Opik (Comet), and Phoenix (Arize) for detailed trace visualization. Step callbacks can implement custom logging. Memory steps are accessible programmatically via agent.memory.steps and agent.memory.get_full_steps().
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval | post-review — (1) Pre-approval: step_callbacks on PlanningStep allow human review and modification of plans before execution. (2) Post-review: final_answer_callbacks validate final answers before acceptance. (3) Step-by-step execution: full manual control between every step. (4) Memory inspection: agent.replay() and programmatic memory access for post-run review. No confidence_threshold-based automation — oversight is implemented through developer-defined callbacks.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Hugging Face (private company). The framework is part of the broader Hugging Face open-source ecosystem. No formal standards body governance. Apache 2.0 license allows unrestricted use, modification, and distribution.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) by Anthropic for tool interoperability. Supports A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol) via community wrappers. Uses OpenTelemetry (CNCF standard) for instrumentation and observability. Built on LiteLLM for universal LLM provider compatibility. Contributes to the Hugging Face Hub ecosystem for tool and agent sharing.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: No explicit compliance certifications (no SOC2, HIPAA, or EU AI Act certification). As a lightweight open-source library, compliance responsibility falls on the deployer. The sandboxing options (Docker, E2B, Blaxel) support security isolation patterns useful for compliance. The audit trail via OpenTelemetry supports regulatory auditability requirements. Organizations deploying in regulated industries must implement additional governance controls. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: local | cloud | edge — Pure Python library that runs anywhere Python runs. Local deployment with pip install. Cloud deployment on any VM, container, or serverless platform. Sandboxed execution via cloud services (E2B, Modal, Blaxel) for secure remote execution. Docker support for containerized deployment. WebAssembly (Pyodide+Deno) support for browser-edge deployment. No managed service offering from Hugging Face specifically for smolagents, but can use Hugging Face Spaces for hosting.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: horizontal | fixed — The framework itself is a lightweight Python library with no built-in orchestration for horizontal scaling. Scales via standard Python patterns (multiprocessing, async). Multiple agents can run concurrently. For production scaling, users typically deploy behind standard web frameworks (FastAPI, Flask) with horizontal scaling at the infrastructure level. No built-in autoscaling or serverless support.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Open-source framework: completely free (Apache 2.0). Only costs are LLM API calls and optional sandbox services. LLM costs: GPT-4o-mini at ~$0.15/1M input tokens makes simple tasks cost fractions of a cent. Local models via Ollama or Transformers: zero API cost (hardware only). Code agents use ~30% fewer LLM calls than JSON tool-calling agents, reducing costs. E2B/Modal/Blaxel sandbox costs vary by provider. Hugging Face Inference API offers free tier for some models.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Very lightweight — core library is ~1,000 lines of code. Minimum: Python 3.10+, pip install smolagents. No GPU required when using API-based models. For local models via Transformers: GPU recommended depending on model size (7B models need ~14GB VRAM). Ollama integration allows local CPU/GPU inference. RAM requirements are minimal for the framework itself (standard Python process). Docker-based sandboxing requires Docker installed. Reported 40-60% less computational resources than monolithic agent frameworks.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation via openinference-instrumentation-smolagents package (SmolagentsInstrumentor). Compatible with: Langfuse (open-source, sends traces to /api/public/otel endpoint), Opik by Comet (full tracing and evaluation), Phoenix by Arize (auto-instrumentation for step and call visualization), LangSmith via OpenTelemetry bridge. Also supports MLflow integration for token count tracking.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — built-in via OpenTelemetry standard. Agents emit traces for every step including reasoning, tool calls, code execution, observations, and errors. Traces include timing and token usage per step. agent.replay() provides local trace playback. External platforms (Langfuse, Phoenix, Opik) provide visual trace exploration with drill-down into individual steps.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: beta — smolagents is actively maintained with frequent releases (v1.24.0 as of Jan 2026) and growing adoption (25k+ GitHub stars, 326K+ monthly PyPI downloads). However, it is explicitly designed as a 'barebones' library prioritizing simplicity over enterprise features. It lacks built-in persistence, advanced memory management, and production orchestration features that frameworks like LangGraph offer. Best suited for prototyping, research, and lightweight production use cases. Enterprise production deployments require additional infrastructure for scaling, monitoring, and compliance.

adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: 326,863 monthly PyPI downloads (last 30 days as of Feb 9, 2026). 96,497 weekly downloads. 25,351 GitHub stars. 2,287 GitHub forks. 194 contributors. 362 open issues. Featured in DeepLearning.AI and DataCamp courses. Part of the official Hugging Face Agents Course curriculum. Community-driven with active GitHub Discussions. Less than 14 months old (created Dec 2024) yet among top agent frameworks by GitHub stars.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: open-source (Apache 2.0) — completely free. No paid tier, no managed service, no enterprise edition. All features are freely available. Costs come only from external services: LLM API providers, optional sandbox services (E2B, Modal, Blaxel), and infrastructure.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: AI research and experimentation (lightweight, fast iteration). Rapid prototyping of agent-based applications. Code-driven data analysis and processing pipelines. Document summarization and sentiment analysis. Agentic RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems. Vision-based web browsing automation. Multi-agent research workflows. Educational applications (teaching agent concepts). Travel planning and multi-step reasoning tasks. Integration with Hugging Face Hub ecosystem for ML workflows.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Positioned as the minimalist, code-first alternative in the agent framework landscape. Differentiates through: (1) Radical simplicity (~1,000 lines vs. thousands in LangGraph/CrewAI), (2) Code-first paradigm (Python code as actions, not JSON), (3) Deep Hugging Face ecosystem integration (Hub, Spaces, Inference Providers), (4) Academic/research backing (multiple papers cited). Weaker than LangGraph for: complex state management, production orchestration, graph-based workflows. Weaker than CrewAI for: role-based multi-agent collaboration, enterprise features. Stronger than both for: simplicity, getting started speed, educational use, and when using Hugging Face ecosystem. Growing fast — from 0 to 25k stars in ~14 months.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: 25,351 GitHub stars, 194 contributors, 2,287 forks, 362 open issues. Active GitHub Discussions forum. Part of broader Hugging Face community (one of the largest AI communities with millions of users). Hugging Face Discord includes smolagents discussions. smolagents organization on the Hub for sharing community tools. Project is only ~14 months old but growing rapidly.
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: good — Comprehensive official documentation at huggingface.co/docs/smolagents covering: conceptual guides (intro to agents), guided tour, tutorials (tools, memory, secure execution, building good agents), examples (multi-agents, plan customization, web browser), and API reference. Also available at smolagents.org (mirror). Includes code examples throughout. Some community reports of documentation lagging behind rapid development (e.g., ManagedAgent docs referencing removed classes).
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: Growing ecosystem. MCP server compatibility opens access to hundreds of MCP tools. LangChain tool compatibility. Thousands of Hugging Face Hub Gradio Spaces usable as tools. Observability: Langfuse, Opik (Comet), Phoenix (Arize), LangSmith, MLflow. Sandbox providers: Blaxel, E2B, Modal, Docker, WebAssembly. LLM providers: 100+ via LiteLLM. No formal plugin marketplace — integrations are via Python code.

(2) Official Hugging Face Agents Course (free, comprehensive, covers smolagents in Unit 1 and Unit 2). (3) DataCamp course: 'AI Agents with Hugging Face smolagents'. human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: assistant (executes with approval) | autonomous (acts independently) — Default: autonomous within max_steps. With step_callbacks on PlanningStep: assistant mode where human reviews plans. With step-by-step execution: fully controlled mode. Configurable per deployment via callback registration.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Via callbacks — step_callbacks pause execution for human intervention (e.g., after PlanningStep). Human can modify agent memory (agent.memory.steps) and resume. final_answer_callbacks allow human review before answer delivery. Step-by-step execution mode provides explicit handoff points at every step. In multi-agent setups, manager agent delegates to managed agents programmatically via code generation — no cross-framework handoff protocol. No built-in UI for handoff — developers integrate with their own interfaces.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Limited built-in support. Within a single run: agent self-corrects based on error observations (failed code execution feeds error back into reasoning). Across runs: no built-in learning or feedback persistence (no episodic memory, no RLHF). Developers can implement feedback by: (1) modifying system prompts based on past performance, (2) using step callbacks to log performance metrics, (3) transferring memory between agent instances. The framework's simplicity means feedback mechanisms are left to the developer.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: High applicability for early-stage startups and prototyping. USE WHEN: (1) You want to prototype agent-based features in hours, not days — smolagents requires as few as 3 lines of code to run an agent, (2) Your team is comfortable with Python and values simplicity over configuration, (3) You are already in the Hugging Face ecosystem (using Hub models, Spaces, datasets), (4) You want code-first agents that naturally compose functions and logic, (5) Budget is minimal — the framework is free and can run with local models (zero API cost), (6) You need multimodal agents (vision, audio, video inputs). AVOID WHEN: (1) You need production-grade orchestration with state persistence and recovery (use LangGraph), (2) You need role-based multi-agent teams with enterprise features (use CrewAI), (3) You need built-in memory, persistence, and long-running agent workflows, (4) Your use case requires formal compliance certifications. STARTUP ADVANTAGE: Apache 2.0 license, zero cost, ~1,000 lines of code to understand, backed by Hugging Face (credibility + ecosystem), excellent learning resources (free courses from DeepLearning.AI and Hugging Face). The code-first paradigm is more transparent and debuggable than JSON-based tool calling.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUILD with smolagents when: you want maximum simplicity, your agents are code-centric (data processing, analysis, computation), you value transparency and debuggability, and you're already using Hugging Face models. The ~1,000 lines of core code mean you can read and understand the entire framework. ALTERNATIVE: LangGraph for complex stateful workflows and production orchestration. CrewAI for role-based multi-agent teams with enterprise SaaS path. OpenAI Agents SDK if locked into OpenAI ecosystem. Cost comparison: smolagents + local Ollama model = $0/month vs. LangSmith paid tiers or CrewAI AMP at $99+/month. The trade-off is simplicity (smolagents) vs. features (LangGraph/CrewAI).
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects) — smolagents exemplifies the Build approach in Build vs Buy decisions, showing how minimal code can create functional agents. Also relevant to Session 5 (agentic AI, code execution safety, sandboxing as a security concept). Minor relevance to Session 4 (open-source business models — smolagents is fully open-source with no paid tier, relying on Hugging Face's broader business model).

confidence.data_quality: High — based on official Hugging Face documentation (huggingface.co/docs/smolagents), GitHub API-verified repository statistics, PyPI download stats via pypistats.org API, official blog post by Aymeric Roucher, and reputable tech sources (DataCamp, KDnuggets, Analytics Vidhya, DeepLearning.AI, ZenML). Release information confirmed via GitHub Releases API.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub API confirms 25,351 stars, Apache-2.0 license, 194 contributors, 2,287 forks (Feb 9, 2026). PyPI Stats API confirms 326,863 monthly downloads. Version 1.24.0 confirmed via both GitHub Releases and PyPI. MCP support confirmed by official docs and community tutorials. DeepLearning.AI course confirmed by Andrew Ng's X post and course listing. A2A support confirmed via community wrappers (any-agent project) and HuggingFace posts. Sandboxing options confirmed by official documentation with detailed code examples.
confidence.caveats: The framework is very young (~14 months old) and evolving rapidly — APIs may change between versions (e.g., ManagedAgent was removed in v1.8.0, later APIs restructured). The 'beta' production readiness assessment reflects its minimalist design philosophy rather than instability. Monthly download counts (326K) include CI/CD automation and may overstate human adoption. A2A support is community-driven, not an official first-party feature. The framework intentionally lacks features that competitors have (persistence, enterprise dashboard, compliance certifications) — this is a design choice, not an oversight. Documentation sometimes lags behind code changes.
